spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Ramanujan-type local bounds create a half-plane in which omitted ramified Euler factors cannot cancel zeros of the partial L-function. This converts uncertain bad-place data into a controlled irrelevance and lets restricted-support zero statistics depend on partial rather than completed L-functions.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Under Ramanujan, each local factor has no pole for Re(s)>0; under a bound toward Ramanujan the pole-free region becomes Re(s)>θ. A zero of the partial L-function in that region therefore survives in the completed L-function. Once the family invariants are known, Conjecture 2 can be checked for support whose size is governed by the quantitative equidistribution estimate, and sufficiently large finite-place-constrained spectral subsets retain the invariants.
directed.conceptual_reading: The move is to separate a robust zero-bearing global object from delicate ramified factors by proving noncancellation in the region being measured. It also makes Fourier support an explicit resolution budget supplied by equidistribution quality.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The partial Euler product L^S and a pole-free half-plane bridge local Ramanujan control to global zero statistics; the family invariants then bridge equidistribution to symmetry type.
directed.boundary_or_failure: Analytic continuation of the partial L-functions is still required, the zero comparison is only justified in the stated pole-free region, and the result remains restricted-support. Large enough is not quantified in this span.
directed.uncertainty: The extraction renders the numerical bound as θ < 21, which is visibly formula-unsafe; the intended fraction and any exact inequality must be checked against the scan before quotation.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: This example separates three layers that can otherwise be conflated: SU(2) local equidistribution fixes the coarse family type, ramified Plancherel mass controls the root-sign split, and only sufficiently wide Fourier support makes the sign-conditioned low-zero laws distinguishable.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: For holomorphic cusp forms of weight k≥2 and square-free level, the family has the SU(2) Sato–Tate measure and indicators i1=i2=1, i3=-1, hence essential symplectic type. The root-number subfamilies have equal proportion, with the split read from the two Steinberg possibilities at primes dividing the level. After removing the forced central zero from the negative-sign subfamily, one-level density gives SOeven and SOodd predictions; support (-1,1) is unconditional, while GRH for Dirichlet L-functions extends it to (-2,2).
directed.conceptual_reading: Family symmetry and functional-equation sign are related but distinct information. The support threshold is an observability threshold: below it several candidate density laws agree, so a correct statistic cannot identify which law generated it.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Plancherel mass at ramified primes feeds the root-number formula, while the SU(2) conjugacy-class measure supplies the indicators. The Fourier support of the test function bridges a limiting density statement to actual discrimination among symmetry types.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The sign-conditioned density removes a forced zero by definition, so it is not the raw zero process. The stronger support uses GRH, and support below one cannot distinguish the three named laws even when the asymptotic is proved.
directed.uncertainty: Several fractions and displayed formulas are degraded in extraction, including 1/2 rendered as 12; the qualitative claims and support intervals are legible, but exact formulas should be scan-checked.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Quadratic twisting acts on the individual Sato–Tate law by averaging it with its image under sign reversal. The full local law can remain as hard as the individual Sato–Tate problem, while just two even trace moments—and hence the low-zero universality type—can be recovered from much coarser pole data.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: For F={π⊗χ:χ quadratic}, scalar multiplication m gives μST(F)=m∗(μ{±1}×μST(π)), equivalently the average of μST(π) and its image under t↦-t. The indicators i2 and i3 become the displayed even trace integrals, while i1=1 by cuspidality. Determining whether the symmetric-square or exterior-square L-function has a pole at one suffices to determine the homogeneous type even when the full individual measure is unknown.
directed.conceptual_reading: A thin transformation can preserve the hard individual distribution problem while compressing the downstream question to a few stable moments. This cleanly distinguishes knowing a measure from knowing only the invariants needed for universality.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The pushforward under C××T→T is the operative representation change. Trace parity explains why sign averaging retains the even moments that encode self-duality type.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The exact pushforward law is stated assuming the individual Sato–Tate conjecture for π, and thinness makes the prime average critical. The source does not claim that quadratic averaging always leaves the individual measure unchanged.
directed.uncertainty: The pushforward mechanism is clear, but the extracted finite-root examples and trace displays are formula-sensitive and should not be quoted character-for-character without the scan.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Enlarging the scalar family from two quadratic signs to the whole unit circle washes out both self-duality indicators. Rich central averaging forces a unitary universality class even though the fixed cuspform may retain complicated individual structure.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: For twists by all Dirichlet characters up to growing conductor, μST(F′) is expected to be the pushforward of Haar measure on S¹ times μST(π) under scalar multiplication. Cuspidality gives i1=1 and circle averaging gives i2=i3=0, so the family is essentially unitary and has U(∞) symmetry independently of π. The associated group is described as generated by Hπ and C× when Hπ exists.
directed.conceptual_reading: A sufficiently rich group action can erase selected invariants of each member without erasing the members themselves. Infinite central variation is the structural reason the family-level view becomes universal.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Scalar convolution/pushforward by S¹ turns individual local parameters into a family distribution; integrating nonzero scalar weights over the circle annihilates the relevant trace moments.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The full group description assumes an individual Sato–Tate group Hπ, and the measure formula is presented as expected. The contrast with the thin quadratic family is essential: it is not evidence that every twisting family forgets individual structure.
directed.uncertainty: Low; the main transformation and indicator values are explicit, although one contragredient symbol in the pole statement is degraded by extraction.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Tensor-product representations make Frobenius–Schur behavior compositional: traces factor and the third indicator multiplies. The degree-six example also shows that fixed even root number is not by itself the explanation of symmetry type.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The family π×sym²(f) is automorphic on GL(6), self-dual symplectic, and has root number +1 for every member. Under individual Sato–Tate for π its measure comes from the tensor embedding SU(2)×PSU(2) into U(6); trace factorization gives i1=i2=1 and i3=-1. Restricted-support one- and two-level densities establish SOeven symmetry in the cited work. More generally the source expects i3(F1×F2)=i3(F1)i3(F2) for suitable homogeneous families.
directed.conceptual_reading: Tensor product is not merely a way to make larger L-functions: it transports symmetry through a multiplicative invariant. The fixed-sign example falsifies the shortcut that low-zero symmetry is only a classification of functional-equation signs.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The map (θ1,θ2)↦θ1⊗sym²θ2 and the identity tr(A⊗B)=tr(A)tr(B) bridge product representations to product moment indicators.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The full limiting measure assumes Sato–Tate for the fixed π, whereas the indicator computation needs less pole information. The general multiplication rule is an expectation for essentially cuspidal homogeneous families, not proved here in unrestricted generality.
directed.uncertainty: Medium-low; the structural formulas are legible, but the extracted central-point fraction is damaged.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Invariant bilinear forms predict adjoint and spin family types, but the statistic can be changed by the measure used to sample the family. Central-L-value weights introduced by a trace formula are not neutral bookkeeping: they can manufacture an apparent symmetry inconsistent with the intended unweighted family.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: An adjoint representation preserves the symmetric nondegenerate Killing form, leading to essentially orthogonal adjoint families and predicted Sp(∞) low-zero symmetry. For the PGSp(4) spin family, the spin representation is symplectic, the indicators are i1=i2=1 and i3=-1, noncuspidal Saito–Kurokawa lifts are negligible, and parity of the weight fixes the root number. The cited low-zero calculation is weighted by fluctuating central L-values, and the source says those natural Petersson weights must be removed to interpret the family symmetry.
directed.conceptual_reading: Representation type supplies the structural prediction, while sampling weights define which population is actually observed. A natural analytic weight can therefore be a confound rather than an innocuous proof device.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The Killing form and the embedding Spin(5,C)≃Sp(4,C) expose orthogonal versus symplectic self-duality. Trace-formula weights form a second bridge—from tractable sums to a reweighted family—that must be inverted before comparison with the conjecture.
directed.boundary_or_failure: Several conclusions are predictions from the conjectural framework; the cited spin zero statistics are weighted and do not establish the unweighted symmetry. Negligibility of exceptional lifts is specific to this spectral family.
directed.uncertainty: Medium; the qualitative weighting warning is explicit, while representation notation and the exact weighting formulas remain extraction-sensitive.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: A universal local measure can be decomposed into conductor strata of Plancherel measure, yet an arithmetic exhaustion can prevent that vertical measure from converging. Low-zero universality may survive because it is a different, deeper aggregate rather than a formal consequence of the local coefficient limit.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: For the universal GLn family the local measure is expected to be an explicit linear combination of Plancherel measure restricted to conductor-powers. The GL(1) case gives a concrete mixture. In contrast, forms restricted to levels n! or successive prime products fail the Sato–Tate limit in the form of equation (5), while low-lying-zero universality is still expected and is stated as verified in specified GL(1), GL(2), and general settings by the cited works.
directed.conceptual_reading: The unit separates two limit procedures: convergence of local parameters under an exhaustion and universality of rescaled zeros. Failure of the first is therefore not logically inherited by the second.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Conductor-stratified Plancherel measures decompose the universal local distribution; changing the sequence of conductors changes the mixture seen by vertical averaging.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The source does not derive low-zero universality from the failed local limit and explicitly says deeper reasons are needed. The scope and hypotheses of the cited proofs are not contained in this span.
directed.uncertainty: The exact GL(1) coefficients are visibly degraded by extraction and should be scan-checked; the counterexample and separation of conjectures are clear.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The decisive compression is residue-class localization: away from the discriminant, a local parameter depends only on w mod p. An infinite lattice average is thereby replaced by a finite atomic measure, and ramification becomes an O(1/p) boundary contribution.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: A smooth proper family X→W supplies cohomological Galois representations and Weil–Deligne local factors. For unramified fibers, the parameter tw,p depends only on w modulo p, so μp(F)|T is the normalized sum of Dirac masses over W(Fp) with D(w) nonzero. Lang–Weil makes the omitted ramified mass O(1/p), and equidistribution of lattice points in residue classes turns the height-ordered integer average into this finite-field measure.
directed.conceptual_reading: Localization makes a global counting problem controllable by a finite quotient while preserving precisely the local parameter relevant to Sato–Tate. Avoiding the discriminant is both a geometric regularity condition and an error-control device.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The chain is fiber cohomology→Weil–Deligne data→local Langlands parameter→residue-class Dirac mass. Reduction modulo p bridges the arithmetic exhaustion to finite-field equidistribution.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The argument uses the affine base, sectors avoiding the projective discriminant locus, natural multiplicities, and bounded ramification depth. Unitarity at bad reduction is conditional, and this unit gives an outline rather than all technical estimates.
directed.uncertainty: High for exact determinant and normalization displays because the extraction is formula-sensitive; the residue-class dependence and O(1/p) mechanism are explicit.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: A lisse cohomology sheaf compresses all fibers into one monodromy representation. Purity moves Frobenius classes onto a maximal compact group, and Deligne–Katz equidistribution turns their finite-field counting measures into Haar measure, producing a canonical family group from the proof rather than from the limiting measure alone.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The sheaf R^d f∗Qℓ yields arithmetic and geometric monodromy groups, with Ggeom semisimple and normal in Garith. Under Garith⊂GmGgeom and purity, normalized Frobenius classes lie in a maximal compact Bc of Ggeom. The measures averaging these classes over W(Fp) push forward to μp(F)|T up to O(1/p), and Katz's form of Deligne equidistribution gives weak convergence to the Haar pushforward as p→∞. For large p the geometric monodromy is independent of p.
directed.conceptual_reading: The sheaf is the useful intermediate object: it replaces many unrelated-looking local factors by one group action. The proof also resolves a nonuniqueness problem by privileging the group that actually generates the limiting law.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Fiber cohomology is packaged as a π1(W)-representation; normalized Frobenius conjugacy classes then pass through Bc#→Tc/W to the Sato–Tate parameter space.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The purity-style containment hypothesis, removal of finitely many primes, and geometric connectedness matter. The stated route to low-zero statistics remains limited-support and conditional on modularity of the fibers.
directed.uncertainty: Medium; the weak-convergence mechanism is clear, but the normalization is described only up to an ℓ-adic unit and the extracted compact-quotient notation is delicate.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The same monodromy measures support two inequivalent averaging problems. Averaging Frobenius over prime powers for a fixed scheme tolerates bases for which height-ordered averaging over arithmetic parameters may have no family statistics at all.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Serre's Sato–Tate conjecture for a finite-type scheme averages μpr(G) over prime powers pr<x and, under suitable conditions, follows from the preceding equidistribution result. The authors contrast this with their family conjectures: the scheme statement is expected for arbitrary bases and proved under mild assumptions in the stated non-point case, whereas allowing arbitrary W in parameter-family averages admits counterexamples.
directed.conceptual_reading: Changing the index and measure of averaging changes the mathematical object, even when both averages reuse the same local Frobenius data. Geometric admissibility for one limit is therefore not an automatic admissibility criterion for the other.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The shared bridge object is μpr(G); prime-power aggregation produces the scheme statistic, while parameter-height aggregation produces the family statistic.
directed.boundary_or_failure: This span announces rather than constructs the family counterexamples, which occur in the following section. It does not say every general base fails, only that mild scheme hypotheses do not exclude family failures.
directed.uncertainty: Low; the comparison is textual, though the precise suitable and mild hypotheses are delegated to the cited source.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Parametric families are not closed under seemingly harmless intersection. Equality of two parametrizations creates a general Diophantine fiber product, and a further arithmetic cut can encode an arbitrary recursive set, destroying even the existence of the averages that define family statistics.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Hilbert's tenth problem prevents general control of W(Z) for bases defined by arbitrary equations. The parameter space for F1(W1)∩F2(W2) is the equality locus F1(w1)=F2(w2), hence a general Diophantine set. The explicit construction starts from a polynomial whose integer values encode a recursive subset, maps its square-free parts to quadratic characters, and intersects with the real-field condition to recover that subset; height-ordered statistics such as equation (5) then need not exist.
directed.conceptual_reading: A controlled ambient representation can lose all statistical regularity after semantic conditioning. The obstruction is not complexity of individual L-functions but loss of a lawful parameter geometry.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The equality fiber product bridges Boolean intersection to Diophantine geometry; the square-free-part and quadratic-character map transports arbitrary recursive behavior into an automorphic family image.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The construction blocks a general closure principle, not every particular intersection or arithmetic subfamily. Strong Hardy–Littlewood control is offered as a sufficient kind of replacement, not developed here.
directed.uncertainty: Medium; the polynomial and square-root notation are extraction-damaged, so the exact displayed construction should be checked against the scan, while its encoding role is explicit.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Cutting a harmonic family by bounded field of rationality may either leave a finite exceptional set or reveal an underlying geometric moduli problem. Thus a simple arithmetic predicate does not by itself tell whether the resulting collection is a statistically meaningful family.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The field Q(π) is defined by the automorphisms of C fixing π. Subfamilies with Q(π)⊆K or bounded degree are introduced; under fixed ramification they are conjectured, and in named cases proved, finite. Weight-two rational-coefficient cuspforms identify with elliptic curves and hence nearly fit a geometric family. For higher weights the source discusses a conjectural realization in pieces of Calabi–Yau cohomology, records special evidence, and asks whether the two family conjectures hold whenever the rationality cut is infinite.
directed.conceptual_reading: Field of rationality is a compression predicate with ambiguous geometry: it can select a moduli family, a thin finite set, or an object whose infinitude is unknown. Establishing the population exists at scale precedes asking for its limiting law.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The proposed bridge runs from rational Hecke data to motives in specified cohomological degree and then to geometric moduli; the elliptic-curve case realizes this bridge concretely.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The central question is open, there is no general infinitude criterion, and the authors explicitly resist claiming all rationality-constrained families arise geometrically. Several higher-weight claims are conjectural or conditional on GRH.
directed.uncertainty: Medium-high because the scope mixes proved finiteness results, conjectural motive constructions, and philosophical suggestions; these statuses must remain separate.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Conditioning on a Plancherel-null local type removes the trace formula's ability to isolate the desired spectrum. Before local parameters or zeros can be averaged, even counting the conditioned family as conductor grows becomes a substantive unsolved problem.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The harmonic-family method permits local restrictions of positive Plancherel volume. Fixed cohomological or C-algebraic archimedean types can form finite sets of local representations with measure zero—for example on GLn with n≥3—and then the trace formula cannot effectively isolate them. Examples include weight-one cuspforms and Maass forms at eigenvalue 1/4. Analogous measure-zero constraints may be imposed at finite places, but even the conductor-growth asymptotic is difficult.
directed.conceptual_reading: A mathematically natural conditioning event can be invisible to the ambient averaging measure. The loss is methodological and statistical: the selector has zero mass, so the main harmonic-analysis instrument supplies no stable denominator.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Positive-volume local test sets are the bridge from trace formula to spectral counts; replacing them by singletons or null algebraic loci breaks that bridge.
directed.boundary_or_failure: This is not evidence that Conjectures 1 and 2 are false for such families. Discrete-series restrictions can have positive Plancherel volume and are a stated tractable contrast.
directed.uncertainty: Low for the obstruction; the exact definitions of the cohomological and C-algebraic loci are only sketched in the span.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Naming a desired Sato–Tate group does not construct or count the corresponding automorphic family. Universal H-type classes are largely inaccessible, whereas geometric specialization and class field theory produce smaller families whose type is computable.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The proposed universal class FH consists of cuspforms with individual group Hπ=H, but Hπ is not generally defined and even growth of FH is mysterious. Hilbert irreducibility can specialize geometric H-extensions to parametric subfamilies. For GL(1), characters of fixed finite cyclic order give tractable examples with μST=μH and unitary type for order at least three. Dihedral weight-one packets provide a GL(2) example with symplectic low-zero type in the cited work.
directed.conceptual_reading: Classification by an invariant and generation by a mechanism are different tasks. Constructible subfamilies provide evidence about a type but need not represent the inaccessible universal class.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The relation H↦μH supplies a type-level representation; Hilbert specialization and class-field characters are concrete bridges from group data to countable arithmetic objects.
directed.boundary_or_failure: Most statements about rich universal H-type families are expectations. Geometric subfamilies may or may not have positive proportion, and the dihedral example varies H over a class rather than fixing one group.
directed.uncertainty: Medium; the tractable examples are clear, while general existence, counting, and representativeness are explicitly unresolved.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Restriction of scalars, functorial lift, and automorphic induction compose geometric variation of number fields with spectral variation over each field. The construction also exposes two non-neutral operations: removing a genuinely common L-factor and imposing thin conductor or Galois restrictions.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: For degree-d fields Ki and an L-group representation r of H of degree m, applying r on each dual-group factor gives R for resKi/Q H, and the corresponding lift is r over Ki followed by automorphic induction to GL(md) over Q. This yields degree-md L-functions when the needed functoriality is known. A factor common to every member may be removed. The source then allows conductor shells, prime-conductor restrictions, and mixed examples such as quartic zeta functions with positive proportions of distinct Galois types.
directed.conceptual_reading: Family-building operations can be composed at the representation level, but later arithmetic restrictions change the sampling problem and may mix invariants. A shared factor is removable only because it is constant across the family, not because factorization is generally irrelevant.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The L-group map for restriction of scalars and automorphic induction is the bridge from Ki-local spectral data to GL(md) over Q; factorization exposes common versus varying analytic components.
directed.boundary_or_failure: Functoriality is conditional where not known, factor removal requires a uniform common factor, and the text calls the restrictions technically problematic rather than asserting they preserve either conjecture.
directed.uncertainty: Medium-low; the construction is explicit in prose, though its applicability depends on external functoriality results.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Weil–Deligne data is the local interface that retains exactly the inertia and monodromy information needed at bad primes. Local Langlands then changes representation language without changing L-factors, epsilon factors, or conductors.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: A Frobenius-semisimple Weil–Deligne representation is a triple (V,ρ,N) with finite inertia image and nilpotent N satisfying the Weil scaling relation. Local Langlands gives a bijection between irreducible smooth GLn(K)-representations and such data, preserving local L- and epsilon factors and conductor. The local L-factor is the inverse determinant of geometric Frobenius on the inertia-fixed part intersected with ker N.
directed.conceptual_reading: The correspondence is a loss-controlled representation change: it replaces automorphic local data by linear Galois data while preserving the analytic invariants used globally. The subspace V^IK∩ker N isolates what survives both ramification and monodromy.
directed.representation_or_bridge: recK is the bridge; conductor measures ramification, N records monodromy, and the Frobenius determinant converts the retained subspace into an Euler factor.
directed.boundary_or_failure: This unit defines a local correspondence and does not itself prove global automorphy. Exact normalizations of Frobenius, modulus, Haar measure, and epsilon factors matter.
directed.uncertainty: Medium because superscripts and the conductor integral are extraction-sensitive; the preservation claims and determinant subspace are nevertheless legible.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The proposed geometry-to-automorphy bridge is layered: cohomology produces algebraic Galois representations, local Weil–Deligne functors produce Euler factors, and conjectural global correspondence packages the same factors into an automorphic representation. Uniqueness is comparatively formal; existence and ramified compatibility carry the real burden.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: An algebraic semisimple ℓ-adic Galois representation has Weil–Deligne realizations at finite places, whose local factors form L(s,ρ), with an archimedean factor supplied from Hodge–Tate data. Coming from geometry means appearing as a subquotient of Tate-twisted cohomology of finitely many smooth projective varieties. Conjecture 4 asserts an isobaric automorphic representation with matching completed L-function; Conjecture 5 reformulates this as a bijection between L-algebraic automorphic data and algebraic ℓ-adic representations. Strong multiplicity one and Chebotarev give expected uniqueness, while full local-global compatibility is stronger at ramified places.
directed.conceptual_reading: The bridge decomposes a global reciprocity claim into interfaces with distinct epistemic status. Matching almost-everywhere data can determine an object uniquely without supplying its existence or its behavior at bad places.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The chain is geometric cohomology→Galois representation→WDv→local factors→global automorphic Π, with Tate and modulus twists mediating arithmetic versus unitary normalization.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The main correspondences, the Fontaine–Mazur characterization, and ramified local-global compatibility are conjectural in this generality. The span lists important known cases but does not turn them into a general theorem.
directed.uncertainty: High for exact normalization exponents because the extracted fraction around the L- versus C-algebraic twist is broken; any formula-level reuse should be checked against the scan.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The determinant twist removes cohomological weight and puts good-reduction Satake parameters on the unit circle. At bad reduction the same normalization is only as secure as weight–monodromy, exposing a precise fault line in the definition of a unitary geometric family.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: For degree-d étale cohomology, the automorphic representation Π is replaced by Π′=Π⊗|det|^{d/2}. At good reduction, Deligne's purity gives Frobenius eigenvalues of absolute value p^{d/2}, so the twisted local Satake parameters have absolute value one and Π′p is unitary. At bad reduction, the analogous conclusion follows from the mixed-characteristic weight–monodromy conjecture, which the source states remains open; the discussion extends to cohomological subquotients.
directed.conceptual_reading: Normalization is a structural operation that quotients out predictable weight, but its success depends on purity information. Singular fibers therefore turn a routine-looking twist into a conjectural interface.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The |det|^{d/2} twist bridges pure cohomological Frobenius weights to the unitary automorphic normalization.
directed.boundary_or_failure: Unitarity is unconditional here only at good reduction. At bad primes it is conditional on weight–monodromy, so unitary local membership cannot be silently assumed for the full family.
directed.uncertainty: Low-medium; the sign and exponent d/2 are clear in the span, but surrounding cohomology typography is extraction-sensitive.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Central criticality is converted into a parity condition on motivic rank, then into the sign of a Galois pairing. For even rank the sign theorem forces a symplectic pairing, contradicting the assumed orthogonal type; the obstruction is therefore representation-theoretic rather than a calculation of the central value.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Proposition 6 states that a cuspidal GLn representation that is orthogonal, regular, and C-algebraic has noncritical central point. In the conditional proof, the corresponding pure rank-n motive has weight n-1 and a self-dual pairing. Criticality at the center requires n even. Bellaiche–Chenevier's sign result then makes the ℓ-adic pairing symplectic, which translates back to symplectic automorphic type and contradicts orthogonality. Dirichlet and elliptic examples illustrate the two sides.
directed.conceptual_reading: The proof reframes an analytic admissibility question as a compatibility test among parity, duality, and pairing sign. Criticality would force a representation type excluded by the hypothesis.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge runs from automorphic criticality to motivic weight and Hodge parity, then through the ℓ-adic realization and its pairing sign back to the automorphic orthogonal/symplectic classification.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The proposition's definition is unconditional, but the proof explicitly assumes the motivic correspondence and related motive conjectures. The necessary integrality condition for criticality is not presented as sufficient by itself.
directed.uncertainty: High for the last Hodge-number display, whose duplicated indices are flagged as likely extraction damage; it should not be quoted exactly without scan verification.
